execution.trigger: An attacker can call withdrawFunds from another address using a reentrancy attack.
execution.state_issue: The use of msg.sender.call.value allows an external attacker to trigger the withdrawal function without proper authorization.
execution.exploitable_behavior: The attacker can bypass access control by exploiting the call method.

causality.state: The withdrawFunds function is called from another address with sufficient _weiToWithdraw.
causality.guard: None, as there's no check preventing external calls to this function.
causality.transition: An attacker can trigger line 20 without being the sender.
causality.capability: The attacker can bypass access control by exploiting the call method in line 20.

vulnerabilities.evidence_snippet: require(now >= lastWithdrawTime[msg.sender] + 1 weeks); require(msg.sender.call.value(_weiToWithdraw)()); balances[msg.sender] -= _weiToWithdraw; lastWithdrawTime[msg.sender] = now;

execution.trigger: A withdrawal is attempted within the same week as a previous one.
execution.state_issue: The time check doesn't account for multiple withdrawals in the same week, allowing subsequent withdrawals to bypass the time limit.
execution.exploitable_behavior: An attacker can withdraw funds multiple times within the same week without triggering an alert.

causality.state: Multiple withdrawals occur within a single week.
causality.guard: The time check doesn't prevent multiple withdrawals in the same week.
causality.transition: After one withdrawal, subsequent withdrawals within the same week bypass the time limit.
causality.capability: An attacker can withdraw funds multiple times without triggering an alert.
causality.outcome: Withdrawals are allowed despite not meeting the time requirement.
